As of 215 PM Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... A Heat Advisory has been issued for Thursday 
11 AM until 8 PM. Anomalously hot temperatures are expected to 
persist into Friday and perhaps linger across the south into 
Sat.

A deep subtropical ridge of around 595 dam is firmly 
established over the TN Valley in the 12z H5 RAOBs this morning 
and is forecast to more-or-less remain in place while elongating
across the Carolinas Fri into Fri night. Highly anomalous H850 
temperatures (at- or-above the 99.5 percentile) currently in 
place over the Ohio Valley and southern/middle Appalachians, 
will gradually shift south and into the Carolinas through Fri. 
This pattern is highly favorable for an early September heat 
wave with minimal convective chances due to influence from the 
strong subtropical ridge. 

Low-lvl thicknesses and diabatic techniques continue to line up
with statistical guidance and supports widespread upper 90s 
continuing through Fri. A few locations may reach triple digit 
air temperatures, but widespread greater than 100 degrees is not
expected. Heat index values across the forecast area are 
expected to eclipse 100 degrees on Thursday with 102 to 108 
expected for consecutive hours south and east of the Triad. 
Additively, weak surface winds and abundant sunshine will 
compound the risk for heat related illnesses, especially 
individuals sensitive to the heat or partake in strenuous 
outdoor activities in the afternoon during peak heating. Anyone 
without effective overnight cooling is at greater risk for heat 
illness as several days with anomalously warm overnight lows in
the mid/upper 70s will provide minimal relief from hot 
afternoon temperatures and humid conditions. As such, a Heat 
Advisory has been issued for Thurs (11 AM until 8 PM) and has
been expanded westward comparative to the Advisory currently in
place through this evening. Additional Heat Advisories will 
likely be needed through at least Fri. 

Increasing convective chances, approaching cold front and 
northeast flow in its wake should put an end to the heat by Sun.


KEY MESSAGE 2...A weakness in the anomalous ridge will favor 
isolated to scattered severe storms Thursday evening.

The anomalously strong ridge centered over the southern 
Appalachians Thursday continues to remain in place. However, a 
slight weakness in the ridge pattern takes shape, with model 
guidance increasingly showing a trend toward some late day to 
late evening isolated to scattered convection across our 
northeast zones.

The GFS continues to show a weak disturbance sliding down 
around the northeast part of the ridge, out of WV/VA and 
clipping portions of the northeast Piedmont and Coastal Plain of
central NC late in the day. Storm coverage appears isolated to 
scattered, perhaps enhanced along subtle surface boundaries. SPC
currently has a Marginal Risk of severe storms over our far 
northeast Piedmont and northern Coastal Plain. Timing-wise, this
appears a late-day event, roughly in the 5pm to 11pm time 
frame. Instability is sufficient but shear is marginal around 
25-kt of deep-layer flow. However, certainly could see isolated 
damaging winds as the primary threat given impressive DCAPE seen
in point soundings of 1000-1400 J/kg.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Labor Day weekend through Monday gradually 
trends somewhat more comfortable, with Friday and Saturday 
seeing our greatest storm chances. 

Overall, the extended forecast has not changed drastically from
the past 24 hours or so for central NC. We are continuing to 
track a cold front that will approach late Friday and Saturday, 
pushing through early Sunday from the NE as somewhat cooler high
pressure builds down from the Mid-Atlantic states. Ensemble 
based solutions continue to favor Friday and Saturday as our 
best coverage of storms, with perhaps Saturday more widespread, 
though that will ultimately depend on the position of the front.
During these two days, SPC has a Slight Risk of severe storms 
during the afternoon into the late evening hours, for our 
central and northern areas Friday and central to southern areas 
Saturday. Based on AI/ML guidance, this severe trend has been 
increasing, with a focus on damaging winds as the primary 
threat. This appears to be driven in large part by 30-kt of 
deep-layer shear and instability.

Much of the ensemble scenarios continue to indicate the front 
pushing through Sunday morning or early afternoon, thereby 
shunting most of the convection to our west and south. However, 
lingering isolated to scattered storms could linger over the 
western and southern Piedmont. Interestingly, a third of the EPS
ensemble members show the front hung up over the area, thereby 
keeping storms in the forecast. This scenario is worth 
considering but for now the consensus is drier with highs around
the middle 80s Sunday through Tuesday. Lower humidity is 
favored with cool high pressure nosing down into the area.
